due_when.clears_when: Capture a per-trade handle for Alpaca protective legs at ENTRY, so identification stops depending on quantity. Either (a) persist the OCO parent/child order ids onto the trade row through the columns that already exist (`trades.sl_order_id` / `tp_order_id`) by widening `execute.execute_pkg`'s capture beyond the Bybit-partial gate, or (b) set a deterministic `client_order_id` on the protective legs at placement — the Alpaca analogue of IB's `oca-protect-t<trade_id>` — and look legs up by it. THEN make `AlpacaClient.modify_protective` prefer that handle and fall back to the qty heuristic only when the handle is absent (pre-migration rows). RESOLVED WHEN a modify on a symbol holding TWO simultaneously-open Alpaca rows OF EQUAL SIZE is observed patching only the named trade's leg — which is precisely the case that returns retCode 1 today, so the current refusal is the positive control and must be shown flipping. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: the qty-scoped path passing its unit tests, which is what already ships. ⚠️ NOT sufficient either: a modify succeeding on a symbol whose rows differ in size — the heuristic already handles that and such a pass proves nothing about the gap.
